description: Decoupled search solves planning tasks whose variables split into a *center* and several *leaves* that interact mostly through the center (a *star topology*). A *leaf action* changes one leaf and reads only that leaf and the center; the search branches over the other, *global* actions only. Each node, a *decoupled state*, holds a center state and, per leaf, the *price* of each reachable leaf state: the cheapest cost of leaf actions that reach it along the path. This removes the interleavings of independent leaf moves, which can shrink the search space exponentially. The result is an ordinary sequential plan, optimal under uniform-cost search or A* with an admissible heuristic.
